minutes.headline: Sewer Commission began drafting new sewer regulations for accessory dwelling units after meeting with town counsel
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission recapped a morning meeting with town counsel about how the new state ADU law affects sewer regulation — tie-in fees, easements, water meters, and septic-to-sewer conversions — and agreed to start drafting its own regulation, comparing notes with Leominster and Fitchburg. It also voted to credit a resident for a water-meter billing mix-up at 17 Renny Street and heard a recap of the Touch-a-Truck community event.

votes.motion: Approve a refund/billing adjustment for the water meter mix-up at 17 Renny Street

budget_items.what_was_said: A meter mix-up between two addresses meant the customer at 17 Renny was billed for the wrong usage for several quarters and is owed a credit. The business manager brought the adjustment to the commission for a vote.
A commissioner proposed setting a flat tie-in fee and standard piping requirements for ADU sewer connections rather than deciding case by case.
Leominster reportedly charges an added one-bedroom fee when a bedroom is added to a house rather than a distinct ADU fee; Harvard reportedly has no policy at all.
A commissioner suggested homeowners could rent an ADU for a monthly figure as heard, which he thought would make ADUs increasingly popular.

decisions.decision: Asked staff (Andrew) to start keeping written notes/headings from the ADU discussion (meters, fees, etc.) to build toward a regulation.
Agreed to reach out to Leominster and Fitchburg to see what ADU sewer regulations or fees, if any, they have adopted.
Each commissioner agreed to draft their own notes/ideas for ADU sewer regulations and send them to Andrew rather than one person drafting alone.
Agreed on the process for adopting ADU regulations: draft internally, send to town counsel for review, then hold a public hearing before voting the regulation in.

what_happened.line: Sewer Commission agreed to draft its own regulation covering ADU sewer tie-ins, fees, easements, and septic-to-sewer conversions, after a morning meeting with town counsel.
Each commissioner agreed to write individual notes and ideas for the ADU regulation and send them to staff, rather than one person drafting alone.
The commission voted to approve a billing correction for a resident at 17 Renny Street after a water-meter mix-up between two addresses.
Commissioners agreed to compare notes with Leominster and Fitchburg on any ADU sewer fees or regulations those towns have adopted.
The commission set its adoption process: draft the regulation internally, send it to town counsel for review, then hold a public hearing before voting it in.

why_it_matters: Any resident adding an accessory dwelling unit will eventually face whatever tie-in fees, meter rules, and septic-conversion requirements this regulation sets, once it goes through a public hearing.
A billing correction for one water/sewer account was approved, a reminder that meter records can be checked and fixed when a mix-up is found.
